newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Luzhou Old-cellar says '96 net up 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: China's Luzhou Old-cellar says '96 net up 16 pct.

text.p: Sichuan-based distillery Luzhou Old-cellar Co Ltd said its 1996 net profit rose 15.91 percent to 244.69 million yuan from 211.09 million yuan in 1995.

Turnover hit 964.35 million yuan in 1996, up 34.47 percent compared with 717.14 million yuan in 1995, with net earnings per share rising 15.2 percent to 1.44 yuan from 1.25 yuan, the firm's annual report said.
The rises were a result of higher output of alcoholic beverages, which climbed 23.47 percent year-on-year to 27,400 tonnes in 1996, the report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
The company planned to use 1996 profits to issue a 0.2 bonus share and a cash dividend of 0.5 yuan per share, the report said.
It also planned to make a three-for-10 rights issue, tentatively priced at between five and seven yuan per rights share, based on 169.416 million outstanding shares at the end of 1996, it said.
Both the dividend and rights issue proposals will be presented to the company's annual shareholders meeting on March 31, it said.
The company aimed to use the rights proceeds to expand spirit output and supplement working capital, it added.
